title: Literal prime alphabet: affine permutations for every modulus above 109
question: Can a fixed affine map modulo any integer greater than 109 nontrivially permute the full 29-prime alphabet?
summary: An exhaustive anchor and divisor certificate leaves only identity. Includes all-modulus reasoning, independent checks and counterexamples for relaxed assumptions.

family.title: Literal-prime alphabet transformations
family.question: Which fixed maps preserve the literal Gematria Primus prime palette?

variant.label: Full-palette affine maps; all integer moduli above 109

scope.representation: The 29 stored Gematria Primus prime values, from 2 through 109; literal values, not rune indices.
scope.procedure: Enumerate distinct anchor outputs of 2 and 3; reduce each nonidentity branch to divisors of nonzero witness differences; verify full palette equality.
scope.parameters: All integer m>109; all coefficient residues a,b modulo m; 812 distinct anchor pairs; no language score.
scope.exclusions: Partial palettes, ordinal/rune-index transforms, noninjective maps, nonlinear maps, and position-dependent keys.

finding: No nonidentity permutation exists within scope: 812 anchor pairs reduce to the identity branch and 13,212 candidate maps with no survivors.
limitations: Full literal-prime alphabet only; not rune indices, partial page support, noninjective maps or position-dependent rules. Human review pending. No proof-assistant rerun.
next_steps: The page-support variant now checks the archived LP2 supports and documents two LP2-55 exceptions. Nonlinear and position-dependent maps require separate tests.

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library; no network or AI. Independent checker: python experiments/records/literal-prime-affine/check.py

review.reviewer: Codex; independent direct modulus-range certificate and exhaustive coefficient controls; human review pending

visuals.caption: Two anchor outputs reduce the infinite modulus range to one identity branch and finitely many divisibility candidates.
